findings.summary: Handler cancellation is not observed on the resident path, so a cancelled or disconnected client leaves a slow request running to its full timeout (retiring the single worker), and the pre-dispatch cancellation check is only ever exercised when a prior request already cancelled admission.
findings.detail: Design section 5 commits that "a timeout or cancellation sends a cooperative cancel frame only when the worker protocol can prove it applies to the active request", and implement.md Phase 3 ticks "exclusive leases, timeout/cancel retirement, crash handling, replacement, and shutdown". The timeout half is implemented (worker/ytdlp_worker.py:271 sends a cancel frame, retires, and the test resident_backend_timeout_is_an_infrastructure_failure_without_retry proves it). The cancellation half has no wiring: the CLI supervisor reacts to client cancellation via the `reply.closed()` select branch and pre-spawn `state.shutdown.is_cancelled() || reply.is_closed()` check (src/supervisor.rs:186, src/supervisor.rs:264), but Backend::reside (src/backend.rs:133-142) only checks `state.shutdown.is_cancelled()` and src/resident_worker.rs never observes `reply.closed()` (its one consumer is supervisor.rs:264). Two concrete consequences: (1) on a cancelled client the task keeps executing; if the client waits for a fresh 503 and retries, the second dispatch is blocked on execution_gate for up to timeout_seconds (default 30s, max 300s) and then times out, retiring the otherwise-healthy single worker and returning 500 WORKER_TIMEOUT. (2) `reside` sends SHUTTING_DOWN when `state.shutdown.is_cancelled()`, but begin_shutdown is only reached by the Drop guard on an unfinished Resources, which requires an interrupted CLI request first - so the branch is effectively unreachable unless the process is tearing down. The design also does not define this resident cancellation contract, so the implement.md checkbox and this finding both rest on an implicit, unverified assumption.
evidence: src/supervisor.rs:264 (reply.closed() branch exists for CLI only)
worker/ytdlp_worker.py:271 (cancel_active_request has no cancellation-frame consumer path in tests)
tests/resident_backend.rs (timeout test present, no cancellation test)
findings.recommendation: Either (a) route cancellation through the manager: oneshot reply closed or state.shutdown observed -> cancel frame to the active request -> bounded grace -> retire worker and reply 503, with a deterministic test using a slow fixture request and a dropped client; or (b) if the Phase 3 ticket genuinely defers cancellation semantics, untick the matching implement.md checkbox, record the gap in the task, and note it in design section 5. As implemented, the current state is neither verified nor explicitly scoped out.

findings.summary: Timeouts surface differently across backends for the same request: CLI returns HTTP 200 with exit_code -1 (per spec error matrix and design section 9), resident returns 500 WORKER_TIMEOUT; resident business errors also surface as 500 with the worker's verbatim code instead of the 200/exit_code-1 shape a client sees on the CLI.
findings.detail: The design (section 9 Compatibility) says timeout compatibility remains HTTP 200 with exit_code -1 "unless a separately reviewed API change is approved", and the wrapper backend spec error matrix rows "Timeout, cleanup succeeds -> 200 exit_code=-1". Backend::reside (src/backend.rs:176-199) returns any non-SHUTTING_DOWN Failure as 500, so the same request that yields {"exit_code":-1,...} on the CLI yields {"error":...,"code":"WORKER_TIMEOUT"} with 500 on the resident backend. The commit's own comment says business codes are surfaced "verbatim" (src/resident_worker.rs:366), which is consistent pass-through but makes the per-backend status/code behavior diverge. Before the resident backend becomes default, design section 9 requires contract tests that "compare resident and CLI results for local deterministic fixtures"; none exists in this commit (tests/resident_backend.rs asserts resident-side statuses only). This is flagged as an open contract question for the review gate rather than a defect: either the difference is an accepted, separately reviewed API change (then record the approval) or the resident path must normalize timeout to the 200/exit_code -1 contract and contract-equivalence tests are added.
findings.recommendation: Decide the timeout/business-error contract for the resident backend explicitly: if 200/exit_code -1 is kept, map WORKER_TIMEOUT (and business errors per the PRD "business-code pass-through" intent) to the RunResponse shape; if divergence is intended, record the reviewed API change and add the resident-vs-CLI fixture comparison tests design section 9 requires.

scope_and_changes_summary: Single commit c08f398 (TEAM B), 16 files, +946/-76. New src/backend.rs defines the Backend enum (Cli default, Resident(Option<Arc<Manager>>)) with from_config/start/shutdown and a reside() execution task that returns the RunResponse contract or an infrastructure Failure. src/main.rs adds --backend/--worker-python/--worker-path/--worker-python-path/--worker-yt-dlp-version (env-backed), builds the backend before admission and fails boot on invalid resident configuration. src/executor.rs routes /run to supervisor::supervise (CLI) or backend::reside (resident) before dispatch and logs the active backend name. src/resident_worker.rs gains per-request temp-dir ownership (RequestTemp, created before dispatch, settled on every path), the run payload now carries request_temp, and worker Error frames surface their business code verbatim. src/resident_worker_manager.rs adds for_config/ensure_started/generation_id/worker_id so the worker starts at boot and is replaced per-request after retirement. worker/ytdlp_worker.py validates the optional request_temp field (fail-closed on empty/unknown fields), borrows the directory by chdir + TMPDIR/TMP/TEMP, and restores cwd/env in a finally. src/models.rs and src/supervisor.rs widen Failure/ErrorResponse code from &'static str to String so dynamic worker codes can pass through. Tests: new tests/resident_backend.rs (5 tests) plus temp-dir and business-code coverage added to tests/test_ytdlp_worker.py (14 tests), tests/worker_protocol_interop.rs, tests/resident_worker.rs, and tests/resident_worker_manager.rs. The only non-source change is implement.md Phase 3 checkbox ticks, which match the delivered state.
